title: Technical Program Manager
description:
SoSafe has the ambition to become the leading human risk management provider in Europe. Our award-winning awareness platform triggers behavioural change by providing effective and engaging training and simulations on cybersecurity and data protection. Cybercrime is costing the world >$10 trillion annually and growing by 15% p.a. - we invite you to be part of the solution!

ABOUT THE ROLE

Platform work at SoSafe carries outsized leverage. One well-run migration touches a dozen services at once. One adopted shared library saves every team that builds on it from solving the same problem twice. One monitoring signal catches a problem before a customer ever sees it. The work often goes unnoticed when it's going well, but its absence is felt across half of Product Development within a week.

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to embed into one of our platform teams and bring order to that complexity. You'll partner closely with the Product Manager, Engineering Manager, and their Tech Leads to drive the when and how of the roadmap: sequencing the work, surfacing risk early, holding cross-team commitments together, and making sure what ships lands cleanly across every team that depends on it.

This role owns program outcomes, not status reports. You'll think in systems, work in mechanisms, and earn trust by removing friction the team didn't know was costing them time.

HERE'S HOW YOU'LL MAKE A DIFFERENCE

- Own end-to-end delivery for programs that touch a dozen services at once: an architecture migration, a compliance remediation, a legacy system sunset.

- Partner with Product Management and GTM stakeholders on platform changes with customer-facing impact, keeping rollouts, communications, and external commitments in lockstep with engineering delivery.

- Drive adoption of shared platform capabilities that other teams are supposed to build on, closing the gap between "we shipped it" and teams actually using it.

- Manage multi-team migrations where downstream consumers, external commitments, and legacy constraints all need to land in the right order. A missed dependency here costs months, not days.

- Run the mechanics that keep a dozen concurrent programs honest: dependency maps, risk logs, decision records, and the recurring check-ins nobody wants to run but everybody needs.

- Bring rigor to how delivery health gets measured, incident counts, adoption rates, time-to-land, and use it to drive change instead of producing another report.

WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT FIT

- You've run complex, cross-functional technical programs and can point to ones where the technical decisions were yours to shape, not just to track.

- You hold your own in deep engineering conversations. You don't need to write the code, but you need to understand what's being argued about and why it matters.

- You bring structure to ambiguity without over-engineering it. Your default is the lightest mechanism that solves the problem.

- You've worked where the consumers of your output are other engineering teams, whether that's infrastructure, data pipelines, or internal APIs.

- You've managed a migration or sunset with real downstream impact, and you know how to land it without breaking trust.

- You communicate directly. Short sentences, clear asks, no filler. You write decisions down and make sure the right people see them.

- You're comfortable in Jira, Confluence, and the rest of a modern engineering toolchain, and you have opinions about how they should be used.

Nice to have

- Background in infrastructure, data engineering, or applied AI/ML platforms.

- Experience inside a SaaS company through a phase of platform consolidation or modernization.

- Familiarity with SLOs or monitoring practice as a delivery signal, not just an SRE artifact.

About the Role

We are looking for a performance engineer who specializes in making large-scale machine learning workloads fast and cost-efficient in the datacenter. This role is focused on distributed training runs spanning many nodes, and high-throughput batch inference sweeping petabytes of real-world autonomy logs for auto-labeling, data mining, ground-truth generation, and evaluation.

The optimization target here is not tail latency on a vehicle - it is throughput, cluster goodput, and cost per unit of data processed. A training run that wastes 30% of its GPU-hours on stalled data loaders, or an offline inference sweep that takes a week instead of a day, directly slows down how fast the whole company can iterate. You will own the gap between what our fleet of accelerators is theoretically capable of and what our workloads actually achieve: profiling across the stack, finding where the compute and the wall-clock time actually go, and closing the difference.

You will work at the intersection of accelerators, ML frameworks, and large-scale data infrastructure, partnering with the teams who own each layer to land wins that show up in training time-to-result and offline processing cost. At Applied, we encourage all engineers to take ownership over technical and product decisions, closely interact with users to collect feedback, and contribute to a thoughtful, dynamic team culture.

At Applied, you will:

- Profile and optimize distributed training end to end - data loading and preprocessing, augmentation, kernel execution, gradient communication, and checkpointing

- Optimize large-scale offline and batch inference over petabyte-scale sensor logs: batching and scheduling strategies, quantization and low-precision execution, graph optimization, and accelerator saturation across long-running sweeps

- Establish roofline and performance models for our workloads, quantify the gap between achieved and theoretical performance, and stack-rank optimization opportunities by impact and effort

- Improve multi-node scaling efficiency: sharding and parallelism strategies, collective communication, interconnect utilization, and memory-bandwidth and kernel-fusion bottlenecks

- Drive cluster goodput - reduce GPU idle time from input pipeline stalls, storage and network I/O, scheduling gaps, stragglers, and failure recovery on long-running jobs

- Build the benchmarking, observability, and regression-detection tooling that keeps performance from silently degrading as models and code evolve

title: Finance Transformation Manager — M-KOPA
description:
Finance Transformation Manager - M-KOPA

You know the difference between a demo and a system that survives contact with a trial balance. That's rarer than you think.
Most people who can talk fluently about AI have never had to make it work inside a real close process, a real audit trail, a real Anaplan model that finance actually trusts. M-KOPA is looking for someone who has - or someone ready to prove they can.
Where this sits. M-KOPA is one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs, now serving 7 million customers across five markets and having unlocked over $2 billion in credit. Behind those numbers is a finance function running on Microsoft Dynamics and Anaplan, increasingly threaded through with Claude, and a leadership team that's decided this is the moment to stop treating AI as an experiment and start treating it as infrastructure.

Why now. We've grown from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we're building toward 10 million next. That growth doesn't just need more finance headcount - it needs a finance function that runs leaner and smarter than the one that got us here. 86% of our customers report improved quality of life , and 70% use our products to generate income ; the systems behind those numbers need to scale without the manual reconciliation and reporting drag that usually comes with scale. This role exists because our leadership has committed to closing that gap now, not after it becomes a bottleneck.
What makes this different. Most "finance transformation" roles are really change-management roles wearing a technical label - you'll sit in workshops, write recommendations, and hand them to someone else to build. This one isn't that. You'll sit inside the finance team, find the friction yourself, and build the fix yourself: deepening our Claude-Dynamics integration, designing agents and workflows that actually replace manual reconciliation work, and owning the result end to end. It's a builder's mandate with a finance brief, not an IT ticket queue.

What you'll bring.

• Demonstrable experience deploying Claude (or a comparable AI system) in a real business context - prompt design, workflow automation, API integration, and artefacts that actually run in production. This is the single most important thing we're looking for, and we'll ask you to show us something real you've built, ideally involving a Dynamics-style integration.

• A technical foundation strong enough to read a data model and a trial balance in the same afternoon, paired with exceptional learning aptitude - the proven ability to apply AI and engineering thinking to genuinely complex financial and accounting scenarios.

• Working knowledge of how audit actually works in practice: mining and structuring data for external and internal audit processes, and following through on remediation of findings, not just producing the report.

What the work looks like. Some weeks you're deep in the weeds of a Dynamics-Anaplan integration, chasing down why two systems disagree on a number. Other weeks you're building an agent that turns a two-day reconciliation into a two-hour one, then coaching the finance team on when to trust it and when not to. You'll be the person finance calls when something's slow, and the person engineering calls when they need someone who actually understands what a close process demands. Data integrity - one source of truth across the finance stack - sits with you.
Reality check. This role asks you to be genuinely bilingual between finance and engineering, and there's no playbook to hand you - you'll be writing it as you go, often while systems are live and numbers are due. If that sounds like friction rather than freedom, this probably isn't the role. If it sounds like exactly the kind of problem you've been waiting for someone to hand you, you're probably ready for it.

title: Permitting Coordinator
description:
Remote Raven is recruiting a full-time, fully remote Permitting Coordinator on behalf of our client, a fast-growing US roofing and exteriors group that runs a family of regional brands across the Eastern and Central United States. The group operates a portfolio of regional roofing brands and completes a high volume of residential and commercial roofing work every year, all of which is regulated at city, county and state level.
The Permitting Coordinator owns the full lifecycle of permit acquisition and compliance across every one of the group's branded entities. You are the central liaison between municipalities, internal teams, homeowners and contractors, and you are responsible for making sure every project meets local, county and state regulatory requirements. You maintain the records, you make the inspections happen on time, and you provide the administrative and operational backbone of permitting across new installations, repairs and warranty work.
This is a role of consequence rather than volume alone. A permit that lapses before its final inspection creates a compliance problem for the brand and a property-record problem for the homeowner, and it does so silently. The person who succeeds here is the one who treats an open permit as unfinished business until the day it is closed.
Key Responsibilities
Permit Application & Expediting

• Prepare, apply for, and expedite permit applications for roofing projects across all of the group's branded entities.

• Identify the correct permitting authority for each project address, including the distinction between an incorporated city and the unincorporated county surrounding it.

• Assemble complete application packets: scope of work, project documentation, contractor license and registration details, certificates of insurance, and bonds where the jurisdiction requires them.

• Submit applications through each jurisdiction's channel, whether that is an online portal, an email intake address, or a phone-and-fax counter.

• Push stalled applications forward: follow up on review times, answer plan-reviewer questions, and resolve corrections and resubmittals.

Tracking, Renewals & Inspections

• Maintain a comprehensive tracking system covering every open permit across every brand and jurisdiction, with status, dates, fees, and next action visible at a glance.

• Ensure timely renewals so that no permit lapses while a job is still open.

• Schedule and confirm final inspections, and confirm every inspection requirement is completed before the permit expires.

• Track failed inspections through to a passed re-inspection, including routing correction notices to the right project manager and rescheduling.

Municipal & Internal Liaison

• Act as the primary point of contact between local authorities and project managers on all permit matters.

• Call, email, and follow up with city, county, and state building departments during their business hours.

• Coordinate with project managers, field crews, the licensing team, and subcontractors to gather the documentation each application requires.

• Communicate professionally with homeowners and public officials, representing the brand on every contact.

Compliance Review

• Review project plans, scopes, and supporting documentation to confirm they meet local permitting and zoning requirements before submission.

• Compile and maintain current knowledge of municipal code years, permit requirements, fee schedules, and inspection protocols for every jurisdiction the group works in.

• Flag scopes that will not pass review as written, before they become a rejected application and a delayed crew.

Close-Out & Problem Resolution

• Own each permit through to close-out, so that jobs finish with a passed final inspection and a closed permit on record.

• Address expired permits by reapplying, resolving outstanding fees, and scheduling follow-up inspections.

• Escalate blockers early and in writing, with the specific action needed and from whom.

title: Engineering Manager, Intelligent Platforms (all genders)
description:
HelloFresh Group is the world's leading integrated food solutions provider, with a global portfolio of brands spanning meal kits, ready-to-eat meals, and specialty products. From our Berlin headquarters, we build and run the technology that delivers millions of meals every week.

We welcome team players who thrive in a dynamic environment, lead with ownership, and bring diverse perspectives to the table. If you are motivated to grow in a culture that champions speed and agility, data-driven decision making, and customer centricity, we would like to hear from you.

The role

The Foundations Alliance builds the tools and infrastructure that empower engineering teams across HelloFresh. Cloud Runtime sits at the center of it: we provide a reliable and highly performant multi-cluster container platform so that every HelloFresh engineer can deploy services with 99.99% uptime, high performance, low latency, and minimal operational overhead.

As Engineering Manager for Cloud Runtime, you will lead a squad of platform engineers who own the container platform, networking, and traffic routing that more than 1,000 production services depend on across Europe, North America, and Australia and New Zealand. You will partner closely with our Product Manager to turn a defined platform strategy into a roadmap the team can execute, and you will be accountable for the reliability and cost of what we run.

This is a hands-on leadership role. Your day will not be spent writing code, but you will be close enough to the system to read a pull request, follow a debugging session, and challenge the team on any technical decision they bring you, from an architecture proposal to an incident postmortem.

What you'll do

• Lead, grow, and support a distributed squad of platform engineers, with team members based in Berlin and Poland, owning hiring, development, and performance for the team

• Build and maintain an engineering roadmap spanning one to two quarters, and make explicit trade-offs between features, timelines, and quality

• Drive our core platform commitments: expanding into a highly available platform with failover between pre-provisioned clusters, increasing adoption of our container platform and multi-region deployments, and reducing infrastructure cost through networking and compute optimisation

• Own the squad's operational metrics and be accountable for moving them

• Facilitate and role-model postmortems, and drive the follow-through on action items

• Manage relationships with key infrastructure vendors and work with Security on audit and compliance requirements

• Partner with the Observability, Release Engineering, and Security squads, where our roadmaps are tightly coupled and dependencies run in both directions

• Foster an inclusive and open working environment, and create the kind of documentation and knowledge sharing that makes the team less dependent on any single person

What you'll bring

• Experience managing a team of engineers, including hiring, performance management, and career development

• Experience leading a team that is split across more than one location, and the habits that make that work

• A strong technical background in cloud infrastructure, with hands-on experience of Kubernetes and at least one major cloud platform

• Familiarity with the surrounding ecosystem: service mesh, API gateways, infrastructure as code, GitOps-style deployment, and secrets management

• The ability to contribute technically when needed, whether that means reviewing code, pairing on a problem, or helping debug an incident

• Experience owning production systems with meaningful availability targets, including incident response and on-call practices

• Judgement about when a decision is reversible and when it is not, and a willingness to front-load design effort on the ones that are not

• Strong stakeholder management, and the ability to say no to a loud request that is not on the roadmap

• Clear written communication and strong async

Compliance, Process Improvement, and Cross-Functional Support
